title: Long idle, short active
hook: A small load lasts many hours. Does duration make it larger than the active load?

knows: that a model can declare hypothetical quantities

misconception: The state lasting the most hours must consume the most energy.

claims.text: Illustrative daily loads: active 60W for 2h, idle 3W for 22h. Constant power is assumed. Scaled model; Illustrative loads: 60 W for 2 hours a day, or 3 W for 22 hours a day; electricity costs €0.30/kWh.
claims.source: Declared hypothetical inputs and limits in resource-specs.json. No actual product, price, tariff, shelf-life, treatment or physical appliance specification is asserted. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: The stage's two results are computed by the printed expressions. At Days=5, A=0.6kWh and B=0.33kWh. Geometry follows the declared dimension relationships. Other pictures use a fixed full scale across the slider range; continuous fills and arcs show relative amounts rather than literal object counts.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["/",["*",60,2,"x"],1000]; B=["/",["*",3,22,"x"],1000]; x denotes Days. At x=5, A=0.6, B=0.33. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. claims.text: For a stated constant load, kWh = watts × hours ÷ 1000. Running cost = kWh × the stated price per kWh; stated fixed costs are added separately.
claims.source: https://www.energy.gov.au/households/energy-rating Australian Government, Energy Ratings, sections Electrical appliances without a star rating / Estimate running costs. Opened 2026-10-13. This supports the general calculation, not the invented model ratings or tariff. | FC pass 35 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED. Definitional, not resting on energy.gov.au (not opened, web blocked): 1 kWh = 1000 W x 1 h, so constant load energy = W x h / 1000; per-kWh cost = kWh x price, with fixed charges separate. Not rendered on this stage (no learner string contains it); the stage formulas apply it: 60 x 2 x 5 / 1000 = 0.6, 3 x 22 x 5 / 1000 = 0.33.

claims.text: Tariffs and appliance ratings vary: check your own.
claims.source: Safety-required stage line (company/reviews/lh-idle-versus-active/2026-10-14-safety.md, lifehacks-safety-reviewer). Source owed: a national energy body or tariff regulator guidance, to be found and checked by the fact-checker. The reviewer named none, and none is asserted here. | FC pass 35 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): HELD. Rendered warning line; the source owed (national energy body or tariff regulator) could not be opened (web blocked). | FC pass 38 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): HELD. Rendered warning line. No source that supports it could be opened from this host: the cited hosts return proxy 403 or fail DNS, and only GitHub raw, PyPI and npm are reachable. I did not verify it from memory or from search snippets. The source is still owed (a national energy body or tariff regulator), and none is named or reachable. As in pass 35: it needs an openable source, or an evaluation-steward ruling on whether a safety hedge is a factual claim.
claims.note: FC pass 50 (fact-checker, 2026-10-15): VERIFIED. Opened two sources myself. (1) Rokicki et al. (2021), 'Differentiation and Changes of Household Electricity Prices in EU Countries', Energies 14(21): 6894, DOI 10.3390/en14216894, publisher abstract read via api.crossref.org/works/10.3390/en14216894 (mdpi.com itself is blocked; abstract only, not full text): the paper sets out 'to identify the differentiation and variation of electricity prices for households in EU countries' (28 states, 2008-2019, Eurostat data) and finds 'higher electricity prices for households in the EU states were associated with better economic parameters', so household prices differ between countries. (2) OpenStax College Physics 2e, section 'Electric Power and Energy' (module m42714, raw.githubusercontent.com/openstax/osbooks-college-physics-bundle/main/modules/m42714/index.cnxml): 'We also think of lightbulbs in terms of their power ratings in watts. Let us compare a 25-W bulb with a 60-W bulb'; a CFL 'puts out the same intensity of light as the 60-W bulb, but at 1/4 to 1/10 the input power'; 'It is easy to estimate the cost of operating electric appliances if you have some idea of their power consumption rate in watts or kilowatts, the time they are on in hours, and the cost per kilowatt-hour for your electric utility' (its worked example says 'If the cost of electricity in your area is 12 cents per kWh'). Together these carry 'Tariffs and appliance ratings vary'; 'check your own' is advice that follows from the OpenStax sentence. The line is hedged and claims no size. Builder: replace the 'Source owed' text with these two citations. Record: company/reviews/lh-idle-versus-active/2026-10-14-fact-check.md, Pass 50. | Previous note: FC pass 41 (fact-checker, 2026-10-15): UNVERIFIED. HELD. Same safety line and gap as lh-duty-cycle-energy c6: no energy-regulator host is allow-listed, and OWID has no household tariff page. Needs a source or an evaluation-steward ruling.
